# Data Dictionary — Fannie Mae Single-Family Loan Performance

**Generated by** `ml/profiling/data_dictionary.py` | schema contract `fnma_sf_llp_113col_v1` | config `1.0.0`

This dictionary enumerates **every one of the 113 positional fields** in the delivered raw files, as required by `dataset_usage.md` §17.3 Rule 3. Fill rates, cardinalities and example values are **empirically observed**, not copied from the published layout — the mapping is evidence-backed.

## 1. Corpus

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Archives | 16 quarterly ZIPs |
| Compressed on disk | 15.21 GB |
| Uncompressed | **205.61 GB** |
| Mean compression ratio | 13.52x |
| Largest single member | 26.51 GB |
| Format | pipe-delimited, **no header row**, 113 positional fields |
| Files profiled for this dictionary | 2018Q1.zip, 2019Q2.zip, 2020Q3.zip, 2021Q4.zip |

Every archive was verified to contain exactly 113 fields before ingestion trusted any positional mapping (`schema_detection.verify_contract`); a width mismatch raises rather than silently corrupting the mapping.

> **Files are never extracted.** 205 GB uncompressed against 56 GB of free disk makes extraction impossible, so every member is streamed directly from its ZIP. See `data/extracted/README.md`.

## 2. Field Classification

Columns are classified into the four functional groups `dataset_usage.md` §17.3 Rule 3 asks for, plus two the raw layout forces:

| Class | Count | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Identifier | 1 | Keys linking the tables |
| Time | 7 | Monthly observation and date fields |
| Acquisition | 29 | Origination-level, constant per loan |
| Performance | 16 | Monthly-varying servicing observations |
| Credit event | 16 | Termination and loss fields |
| Unused | 44 | Present in the layout but empty or out of scope |

**45 of 113 fields are parsed.** Column pruning is the single largest throughput win available: parsing 45 of 113 fields roughly triples read speed over ~870M rows.

**68 of 113 fields are marked verified** — their positional mapping was confirmed against observed value ranges, formats and cross-field consistency. The remainder are consistently empty in this vintage; they are named for completeness and **nothing in the pipeline depends on them**. Three trailing positions (110–112) could not be confirmed against the published layout and are labelled `UNVERIFIED_*` rather than being given a speculative name.

## 4. Schema Bridge — Raw → Canonical

The project documentation (`api_spec.md`, `database_schema.md`, `dataset_usage.md` §4) describes a **curated** schema with fields like `loan_id`, `credit_score_band`, `current_status`, `default_flag`. The delivered data is the **raw** Fannie Mae layout. This table is the bridge between them — the Gap 1 decision in `docs/documentation_analysis.md` §3.

### 4.1 Direct renames

| Raw field | Canonical field | Transformation |
|---|---|---|
| `LOAN_ID` | `loan_id` | strip whitespace |
| `ACT_PERIOD` | `reporting_month` | `MMYYYY` → month-start timestamp |
| `ORIG_DATE` | `origination_month` | `MMYYYY` → month-start timestamp |
| `ORIG_UPB` | `original_balance` | → float32 |
| `CURRENT_UPB` | `current_balance` | → float32, zero-balance repair (§4.4) |
| `ORIG_RATE` | `interest_rate` | → float32 |
| `CURR_RATE` | `current_interest_rate` | → float32 |
| `LOAN_AGE` | `loan_age_months` | → Int16 |
| `REM_MONTHS` | `remaining_term_months` | → Int16 |
| `CSCORE_B` | `credit_score` | → float32, retained alongside its band |
| `OLTV` | `ltv` | → float32, retained alongside its band |
| `DTI` | `dti` | → float32, retained alongside its band |
| `STATE` | `state` | explicit `Unknown` for blanks |
| `SERVICER` | `servicer_name` | explicit `Unknown` for blanks |
| `MOD_FLAG` | `modification_flag` | `Y` → true |
| `FORBEARANCE_INDICATOR` | `forbearance_flag` | not in {blank, `N`, `7`} → true |

### 4.3 Banding — continuous → documented categorical

`api_spec.md` contracts on banded strings such as `"680-719"`, `"80-90"`, `"36-43"`. Cut-points are chosen to reproduce those examples. **The continuous source value is always retained alongside the band**, so the API contract holds while models keep full numeric resolution — banding is additive, never lossy.

**`credit_score_band`** from `CSCORE_B` — left-closed intervals:

| Band | Range |
|---|---|
| `<580` | [0, 580) |
| `580-619` | [580, 620) |
| `620-659` | [620, 660) |
| `660-679` | [660, 680) |
| `680-699` | [680, 700) |
| `700-719` | [700, 720) |
| `720-739` | [720, 740) |
| `740-759` | [740, 760) |
| `760-779` | [760, 780) |
| `780+` | [780, 851) |
| `Unknown` | value missing or unparseable |

| Band | Range |
|---|---|
| `<60` | [0, 60) |
| `60-70` | [60, 70) |

| `Unknown` | value missing or unparseable |

### 4.4 Derived fields — the target-critical logic

Every label in the project descends from **two raw fields**. This is the highest-risk mapping in the build and is unit-tested in `tests/test_targets.py` (25 cases).

**`DLQ_STATUS` → delinquency**

| Raw | Meaning | `dlq_months` | `days_past_due` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `00` | current | 0 | 0 |
| `01` | 30 days | 1 | 30 |
| `02` | 60 days | 2 | 60 |
| `03` | 90 days | 3 | 90 |
| `06` | 180 days | 6 | 180 |
| `12` | 360 days | 12 | 360 |
| `XX` / blank | **servicer did not report** | `NaN` | `NaN` |

`XX` is deliberately **not** mapped to zero. An unreported status is not a current loan, and conflating the two would understate risk. The missingness is preserved, flagged as `dlq_status_unreported`, and surfaced as data-quality rule **R008**.

**`Zero_Bal_Code` → terminal state.** Populated only on a loan's final record, when the balance reaches zero:

| Code | Meaning | Canonical state | Flags set |
|---|---|---|---|
| `01` | prepaid_or_matured | `Prepaid` | `prepayment_flag` |
| `02` | third_party_sale | `Default` | `default_flag`, `default_flag_credit_event` |
| `03` | short_sale | `Default` | `default_flag`, `default_flag_credit_event` |
| `06` | repurchased | `Closed` | — |
| `09` | deed_in_lieu_reo | `Default` | `default_flag`, `default_flag_credit_event` |
| `15` | note_sale | `Default` | `default_flag`, `default_flag_credit_event` |
| `16` | reperforming_loan_sale | `Closed` | — |

**Loan state machine.** Terminal codes take precedence over delinquency depth, so a loan that pays off while delinquent is `Prepaid`, not `Delinquent`:

```
if   Zero_Bal_Code == '01'                -> Prepaid   (terminal)
elif Zero_Bal_Code in {02,03,09,15}       -> Default   (terminal, credit event)
elif Zero_Bal_Code in {06,16}             -> Closed    (terminal)
elif dlq_months >= 6                     -> Default   (D180)
elif dlq_months >= 1                     -> Delinquent
else                                      -> Current
```

**Three default definitions are materialised, not one.** COVID-era forbearance pushed many loans past 180 days delinquent without an economic default, because missed payments under an approved plan still accrue as delinquency. Rather than quietly pick one definition:

| Field | Definition | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `default_flag` | D180 **or** credit event | Primary; the documented definition (assumption A4) |
| `default_flag_credit_event` | terminal credit event only | Unambiguous economic default |
| `default_flag_ex_forbearance` | credit event **or** (D180 **and** not in forbearance) | Forbearance-adjusted |

`forbearance_flag` is also supplied as a model feature so the classifier can separate relief-driven delinquency from genuine deterioration.

**Zero-balance repair.** Fannie Mae systematically reports `CURRENT_UPB = 0.00` on a loan's earliest records, before the servicer's first full balance submission — verified: in the 2019Q1 file *every* record in the first reporting month (129,126 rows) carries a zero balance. A zero balance on a non-terminal row is a reporting artifact, not a paid-off loan; feeding it to a model as a real zero would corrupt every balance ratio and make new loans look fully amortised. Repair is forward-fill (mid-history gaps) then back-fill (leading zeros), both flagged via `balance_imputed`; loans whose entire history is zero remain `NaN` rather than being filled with a fabricated number.

## 5. Canonical Output Tables

| `loan_id` | Primary key |
| `original_balance` | Loan amount at origination; denominator for balance ratios |
| `interest_rate` | Origination rate; payment burden and refinance incentive |
| `credit_score` | Borrower FICO at origination (continuous) |
| `credit_score_band` | Banded credit score (API contract) |
| `ltv` | Original loan-to-value % (continuous) |
| `ltv_band` | Banded LTV (API contract) |
| `dti` | Debt-to-income % at origination (continuous) |
| `dti_band` | Banded DTI (API contract) |
| `state` | US state; geographic segment dimension |
| `loan_purpose` | purchase / refinance / cash_out_refinance |
| `property_type` | Decoded property type |
| `occupancy_type` | principal / investor / second_home |
| `origination_month` | Month the loan was originated |
| `original_term_months` | Original term |
| `channel` | retail / correspondent / broker |
| `seller_name` | Selling institution |
| `num_borrowers` | Number of borrowers |
| `co_borrower_credit_score` | Co-borrower FICO (~43% populated) |
| `first_time_buyer` | First-time homebuyer flag |
| `num_units` | Units in the property |
| `msa` | Metropolitan statistical area |
| `zip3` | First three ZIP digits |
| `mi_pct` | Mortgage insurance coverage % |
| `mi_type` | Who pays the mortgage insurance |
| `product_type` | FRM / ARM |
| `homeready_flag` | HomeReady affordable-lending program |
| `high_balance_flag` | High-balance loan indicator |
| `vintage_year` | Origination year; vintage segment dimension |
| `vintage_quarter` | Origination quarter |
| `source_file` | Originating quarterly archive (lineage) |

### 5.2 `loan_monthly_performance.parquet` — one row per loan-month

| Column | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `loan_id` | Foreign key to loans |
| `reporting_month` | Observation month; drives the time-aware split |
| `month_index` | Derived per-loan sequential counter from 0 |
| `loan_age_months` | Months since origination; survival duration clock |
| `current_balance` | Outstanding principal (zero-balance repaired) |
| `current_interest_rate` | Current rate |
| `remaining_term_months` | Months to scheduled maturity |
| `days_past_due` | dlq_months x 30 |
| `dlq_months` | Months delinquent from DLQ_STATUS |
| `current_status` | Current / Delinquent / Default / Prepaid / Closed |
| `delinquency` | dlq_months >= 1 |
| `default_flag` | D180 or credit event (primary definition) |
| `prepayment_flag` | Zero_Bal_Code = 01 |
| `modification_flag` | Loan was modified |
| `zero_balance_code` | Raw termination code |
| `zero_balance_date` | Termination month; event date for survival analysis |
| `last_upb` | Balance immediately before termination; exposure at default |
| `scheduled_principal` | Total scheduled principal paid |
| `non_interest_bearing_upb` | Deferred balance; forbearance signal |
| `principal_forgiveness` | Principal forgiven; modification severity |
| `forbearance_flag` | Loan is under a forbearance/loss-mitigation plan |
| `servicer_name` | Current servicer; segment dimension |
| `last_paid_installment` | Date of last paid installment; staleness signal |
| `is_terminated` | A terminal zero-balance code is present |
| `termination_reason` | Decoded termination reason |

### 5.3 Join logic

```
loan_static_attributes  ──┐
                          ├── join on loan_id ──> loan-month panel
loan_monthly_performance ─┘        (1 row = 1 loan at 1 month)
```

`month_index` is **derived**, not present in the raw data: a per-loan sequential counter over sorted `reporting_month`, starting at 0 (assumption A8). It is computed during the streaming pass, which is exact because loan sets are disjoint across quarterly files and a loan's rows are contiguous and month-ordered within a file — both verified empirically.

## 6. Assumptions

| # | Assumption | Basis | Risk if wrong |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | The 113 positional fields follow the published Fannie Mae layout | Every position profiled; value ranges, formats and cross-field consistency agree | Mis-mapped features — mitigated by profiling plus derived-field unit tests |
| A2 | `DLQ_STATUS` is months-delinquent as a 2-char code | Observed value set {00..18, XX} with the expected monotone frequency decay | Wrong delinquency labels; highest-impact risk, unit-tested |
| A3 | `Zero_Bal_Code` 01=prepaid, {02,03,09,15}=credit event, {06,16}=closed | Fannie Mae published code list; `01` dominant as expected | Prepayment and default inverted — two economically opposite outcomes |
| A4 | Default = 180+ days delinquent or a credit event | Industry-standard D180; `prd.md` says "a defined default state" without fixing it | Shifts the base rate; all three definitions are reported |
| A5 | Band cut-points for credit score / LTV / DTI | Chosen to reproduce the literal examples in `api_spec.md` | Cosmetic only — continuous values are retained |
| A8 | `month_index` is a derived per-loan sequential counter | `dataset_usage.md` §4.1 defines it as such; absent from raw data | None — derived deterministically from sorted `reporting_month` |
